title.value: B LOCK C ONTEXTUAL MDP S FOR C ONTINUAL L EARNING
title.justification: The title is directly mentioned at the beginning of the paper before the abstract.
title.quote: B LOCK C ONTEXTUAL MDP S FOR C ONTINUAL L EARNING Anonymous authors Paper under double-blind review

extractions.description: This paper addresses the challenges of nonstationarity in reinforcement learning by proposing a Block Contextual MDP framework. It challenges RL algorithms to handle nonstationarity and rich observation settings, also providing generalization bounds using Lipschitz properties. Inspired by adaptive control, the paper introduces a novel algorithm called ZeUS for zero-shot adaptation at evaluation time in nonstationary environments.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning, continual learning, and nonstationary environments. While these concepts can be indirectly related to optimizing systems that may impact climate change (like adaptive control in real-world settings), climate change itself is not the central theme of the paper.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In the more extreme cases, even the observation and action space can change over time. These setups are commonly grouped under the continual learning paradigm and non-stationarity is incorporated as a change in the task or environment distribution.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address climate change or any specific climate change category. It focuses on reinforcement learning and the challenges of nonstationary environments, which are not explicitly linked to climate change in the paper.
primary_category.quote: In reinforcement learning (RL), when defining a Markov Decision Process (MDP), the environment dynamics is implicitly assumed to be stationary. This assumption of stationarity, while simplifying, can be unrealistic in many scenarios.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no direct sub-category applicable as the content focuses on reinforcement learning without explicit reference to climate change.
primary_sub_category.quote: This assumption of stationarity, while simplifying, can be unrealistic in many scenarios.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper is centered around advancing reinforcement learning methods to handle nonstationary environments through a Block Contextual MDP framework and the proposed ZeUS algorithm.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose to model this more realistic, rich observation, nonstationary setting as a Block Contextual MDP (BC-MDP) by combining two common assumptions.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The particular focus of the paper is on continual learning in reinforcement learning systems, a specific facet of applying RL to dynamic, nonstationary environments.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The ability to handle non-stationarity is a fundamental building block for developing continual learning agents.
